name_en: Devilled Beef (Sri Lankan Spicy Beef Stir-Fry)

ingredients.name: Beef steak (sirloin, ribeye, or rump)
ingredients.notes: sliced thinly against the grain into strips; thin slices sear faster and stay tender

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: for the marinade; a key flavour driver in devilled beef

ingredients.name: Dark soy sauce
ingredients.notes: dark soy for marinade gives colour; use light soy for the sauce to keep the sauce glossy red

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: apple cider or white; for the marinade

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.notes: cut into wedges; added at the end so they don't turn mushy

steps.instruction: Slice the beef thinly against the grain into strips about 5mm thick. Marinate with dark soy sauce, vinegar, black pepper, and salt for at least 30 minutes.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or large pan over very high heat. When smoking hot, add the beef in a single layer. Sear without stirring for 1-2 minutes, then toss and stir-fry for a further 2-3 minutes until browned and slightly caramelised. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding -- overcrowding causes steaming instead of searing. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok. Add ginger, garlic, curry leaves, and cinnamon. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the onion wedges, banana peppers, and green chillies. Stir-fry over high heat for 2-3 minutes, keeping the vegetables crunchy.
Add the ketchup, light soy sauce, sugar, curry powder, and chilli flakes. Toss everything together.

Return the beef to the wok. Add the tomato wedges. Toss everything together over high heat for 2-3 minutes until the beef is well coated in the glossy red-brown sauce. Add any leftover marinade at this stage.
Taste and adjust seasoning -- more ketchup for sweetness, more chilli for heat. The dish should be dry and glossy, not wet and soupy. Serve immediately with rice, string hoppers, or bread.

source_site: theflavorbender.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, greatcurryrecipes.net, hr-cookery.ca, cupofyum.com, and nipcooks (TikTok) for sauce ratios and sear technique
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; very strong agreement on marinate-then-sear-then-sauce technique and the ketchup-soy-vinegar-sugar base
notes: Devilled beef uses the identical sauce base as devilled chicken (sl_032), devilled fish (sl_033), and devilled pork (sl_071) -- ketchup, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar -- making it the fourth entry in the Sri Lankan-Chinese devilled dish cluster in this dataset. The key difference from the other devilled proteins is that beef needs a sear-then-set-aside-then-toss approach rather than deep-frying first, since thin beef strips cook very quickly at high heat and will toughen if overcooked in oil. The sear must happen on very high heat in uncrowded batches -- this caramelises the beef and gives it the characteristic slightly charred, crispy edges. Tomatoes are consistently added at the very end across all sources to prevent them from turning watery and diluting the sauce. Like all devilled dishes, vegetables must be kept crunchy.
